chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked him about a man who buys dirhams from another man in exchange for dinars, weighing them, selecting them, and calculating their price in terms of how many dinars. Then he says, 'Send your slave with me so that I may give him the dinars.' He (the Imam) said, 'I dislike that they part company until he takes the dinars.' I said, 'They are in one house and their places are close to one another, and this is difficult for them.' He said, 'When he finishes weighing and selecting them, let him order the slave whom he sends to be the one who conducts the transaction with him, and deliver the silver (dirhams) to him and take the gold (dinars) from him, at the place where he delivers the silver to him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging gold for silver if the parties are in the same house?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the Shia jurisprudence of *sarf* (currency exchange), emphasizing that the exchange of gold for silver must be immediate and in one sitting to avoid *gharar* (uncertainty). The Imam’s ruling that the slave acts as an agent to ensure simultaneous delivery illustrates the principle that physical or constructive possession (*qabd*) must be complete before the contract is finalized, even if parties are in close proximity.
